updates.claim: Discrete topology labels have not earned Agent control authority. Preserve observable causal/evidence affordances and empirical operator priors, but do not require classification into a topology enum before operator selection.
updates.evidenceSummary: Across 18 deceptive-surface trials, open achieved 3/6 correct topology and 5/6 correct owner; surface-locked achieved 0/6 topology and 2/6 owner; topology-challenge achieved 0/6 topology and 3/6 owner while consuming 6.27M tokens versus 4.25M open.

updates.claim: A correct meta-rule in Agent context is not evidence of the corresponding control competence.
updates.evidenceSummary: Explicitly instructing the Agent to treat topology as defeasible did not create reliable reclassification or switching, paralleling TM1 static research-taste prose and HP2 serial stopping narration.

updates.claim: Classifier output must not outrank owner-native causal evidence; a misleading class can remain sticky even after the Agent reconstructs the underlying mechanism.
updates.evidenceSummary: Surface-locked deception produced 0/6 correct topology, 5/6 false localization, and in SEC one trial recovered all hidden causal concepts while retaining the false distributed label.

updates.claim: Operator choice should be conditioned directly on observable research affordances such as stable diagnostic identity, causal co-location, cross-carrier relation, unresolved owner substitution, physical race or ambiguous consequence rather than an authoritative topology enum.
updates.evidenceSummary: HP3 does not invalidate prior TM2/TM3/HP1 operator contrasts; it invalidates the tested topology-label control representation.

rejected: Agent-facing topology enum as an operator control interface
ResearchTasteService or scheduler/query planner derived from HP3
nextFrontier: HP4 should test evidence applicability/revision binding under concurrent owner change. It should not depend on successful topology classification.
